title: Turn Release Down to See the Packets

scenes.tts: If the nerve's response is built from miniatures, why can't you just see them?
scenes.visual: A smooth evoked endplate potential on a trace, with the question beside it.
scenes.narration: If the nerve's response is built from miniatures, why can't you just see them?

scenes.tts: In normal calcium, one impulse releases dozens of units or more at once.
scenes.visual: Split screen, left half labelled normal calcium: a burst of many vesicles fusing together.
scenes.narration: In normal calcium, one impulse releases dozens of units or more at once.

scenes.tts: They merge into one smooth response. It is like a downpour, where you cannot count the drops.
scenes.visual: Left half: one big smooth response on the trace, with a downpour of rain behind it.
scenes.narration: They merge into one smooth response. It is like a downpour, where you cannot count the drops.

scenes.tts: To count drops, you need a drizzle.
scenes.visual: Right half lights: a light drizzle, a few drops at a time.
scenes.narration: To count drops, you need a drizzle.

scenes.tts: So del Castillo and Katz lowered calcium and raised magnesium in the bath around a frog junction.
scenes.visual: Right half labelled low calcium, high magnesium. Names on screen: José del Castillo, Bernard Katz.
scenes.narration: So del Castillo and Katz lowered calcium and raised magnesium in the bath around a frog junction.

scenes.tts: That cut release to a trickle.
scenes.visual: Right half: few vesicles fuse per impulse. Across impulses, often none, sometimes one, now and then two or three.
scenes.narration: That cut release to a trickle.

scenes.tts: Now an impulse often produced nothing at all. That is called a failure.
scenes.visual: Stimulus marks along the trace; many are followed by a flat line, each labelled failure.
scenes.narration: Now an impulse often produced nothing at all. That is called a failure.

scenes.tts: When a response did come, it was small. So they stimulated many times and sorted the sizes.
scenes.visual: Small responses of varied height stack up beside the trace, ready to be sorted.
scenes.narration: When a response did come, it was small. So they stimulated many times and sorted the sizes.

scenes.tts: Picture a histogram. Response size runs along the bottom. The number of trials runs up the side.
scenes.visual: Empty histogram axes draw: response amplitude (mV) along the bottom, number of trials up the side.
scenes.narration: Picture a histogram. Response size runs along the bottom. The number of trials runs up the side.

scenes.tts: If release were a smooth flow, just turned down, what shape would this histogram have?
scenes.visual: The empty axes with the question on screen.
scenes.narration: If release were a smooth flow, just turned down, what shape would this histogram have?

scenes.tts: One simple smooth-flow model would give one smooth spread of sizes, with no regularly spaced peaks. The telling sign of packets would be peaks spaced at one miniature.
scenes.visual: A faint dashed single hump sketches over the axes, labelled illustrative smooth-flow model, no all-or-none step.
scenes.narration: One simple smooth-flow model would give one smooth spread of sizes, with no regularly spaced peaks. The telling sign of packets would be peaks spaced at one miniature.

scenes.tts: That is not what they found. Watch the trials drop in.
scenes.visual: The dashed hump fades. Trials begin to drop into the histogram one at a time.
scenes.narration: That is not what they found. Watch the trials drop in.

scenes.tts: A tall bar builds at zero. These are the failures.
scenes.visual: A tall bar grows at zero amplitude, labelled failures.
scenes.narration: A tall bar builds at zero. These are the failures.

scenes.tts: A bump grows near the size of one miniature. The miniature histogram lines up over it.
scenes.visual: A bump grows at 1 × q. The histogram of spontaneous miniatures, in a second colour, draws over it and lines up.
scenes.narration: A bump grows near the size of one miniature. The miniature histogram lines up over it.

scenes.tts: A smaller bump grows near twice that size. A smaller one again near three times.
scenes.visual: Smaller bumps grow at 2 × q and 3 × q. Tick labels: 0, q, 2q, 3q.
scenes.narration: A smaller bump grows near twice that size. A smaller one again near three times.

scenes.tts: The bumps are broad, because one unit is not exactly the same size every time, and the recording has noise.
scenes.visual: The width of each bump is bracketed. Labels: q varies from packet to packet; recording noise.
scenes.narration: The bumps are broad, because one unit is not exactly the same size every time, and the recording has noise.

scenes.tts: But the sizes cluster near whole-number multiples of the miniature. The response comes in packets.
scenes.visual: Labels 0, 1, 2, 3 packets appear over the bar and bumps.
scenes.narration: But the sizes cluster near whole-number multiples of the miniature. The response comes in packets.

scenes.tts: Each packet is called a quantum. Its effect on the muscle, the miniature, is the quantal size.
scenes.caption: Each packet is called a quantum. Its effect on the muscle, the miniature, is the quantal size, q.
scenes.visual: A vesicle cartoon beside the first bump. Labels: one quantum; quantal size, q = one miniature.
scenes.narration: Each packet is called a quantum. Its effect on the muscle, the miniature, is the quantal size, q.

scenes.tts: A quantum holds thousands of acetylcholine molecules. It was later tied to the contents of one vesicle.
scenes.visual: The vesicle cartoon fills with many small dots. Label: one quantum = one vesicle's contents.
scenes.narration: A quantum holds thousands of acetylcholine molecules. It was later tied to the contents of one vesicle.

scenes.tts: It is not one molecule.
scenes.visual: A single dot is pulled out and crossed through. Label: not one molecule.
scenes.narration: It is not one molecule.

scenes.tts: Think of coins dropped into a jar on a scale. You cannot see the coins.
scenes.visual: A covered jar on a scale; coins drop in out of sight.
scenes.narration: Think of coins dropped into a jar on a scale. You cannot see the coins.

scenes.tts: But if every reading is a multiple of one coin's weight, you can count them.
scenes.visual: The scale reads in steps; each step is labelled 1 coin, 2 coins, 3 coins.
scenes.narration: But if every reading is a multiple of one coin's weight, you can count them.

scenes.tts: That gives the one idea of this lesson. Each response is roughly the count times the size.
scenes.caption: That gives the one idea of this lesson: each response ≈ count × size. On average, EPP ≈ m × q.
scenes.visual: Guiding-idea card: response ≈ count × size; on average, EPP ≈ m × q (m = average count).
scenes.narration: That gives the one idea of this lesson: each response ≈ count × size. On average, EPP ≈ m × q.

scenes.tts: The nerve terminal sets the count. Calcium sets it steeply.
scenes.caption: The nerve terminal sets the count, m. Calcium sets it steeply.
scenes.visual: On the card, an arrow from the nerve terminal to count (m), with a calcium icon beside it.
scenes.narration: The nerve terminal sets the count, m. Calcium sets it steeply.

scenes.tts: One vesicle's transmitter, acting on the receptors, sets the size.
scenes.caption: One vesicle's transmitter, acting on the receptors, sets the size, q.
scenes.visual: On the card, an arrow from a vesicle and receptors to size (q).
scenes.narration: One vesicle's transmitter, acting on the receptors, sets the size, q.

scenes.tts: Big responses fall short of this rule. A later chapter shows why.
scenes.visual: A small note under the card: ≈ because big responses fall short (see chapter 5).
scenes.narration: Big responses fall short of this rule. A later chapter shows why.

scenes.tts: The count is random from impulse to impulse. What we track is its average.
scenes.caption: The count is random from impulse to impulse. What we track is its average, m.
scenes.visual: A row of trials with different packet counts; their average is marked as m.
scenes.narration: The count is random from impulse to impulse. What we track is its average, m.

scenes.tts: So when transmission changes, ask first. Did the count change, the size, or both?
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: response ≈ count × size. Did the count change, the size, or both?
scenes.narration: So when transmission changes, ask first. Did the count change, the size, or both?
